messages.author: 082a41d3901aa197
messages.subject: Mediation muddle
parts:
Does the following scenario surprise anyone? It is my situation, which I am a bit perplexed by. 


Using JASP, which runs lavaan:

I have a situation where Predictor 1 is shown to have an indirect effect, via Mediator, on dependent variable. 

And when tested seperately, Predictor 2 is shown to have an indirect effect, via the same Mediator, on the same dependent variable.

But when Predictor 1 is multiplied by Predictor 2, to create a new Predictor variable, we will call Predictor X. This is NOT observed to have an indirect effect. This runs against my expectation.  

Moreover, when Predictor 1 and Predictor2 are tested Together as predictors - there is no indirect effect observed for either.  

Is it just that my expectations are ill placed?

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: Mediation muddle
parts: This part:
"Moreover, when Predictor 1 and Predictor2 are tested Together as predictors - there is no indirect effect observed for either."

Is not at all surprising if 1 and 2 are correlated.It's the same shared variance issue as in any multiple regression framework.

This part:
"But when Predictor 1 is multiplied by Predictor 2, to create a new Predictor variable, we will call Predictor X. This is NOT observed to have an indirect effect. This runs against my expectation."

The most likely scenarios here are that the test is under-powered or your hypothesis about X is incorrect. Are 1 and 2 included in the model with X? If not, they should be. Again, same as in any multiple regression.

Pat

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: Mediation muddle
parts:
In a regression framework, if you include a higher-order term (e.g., a two-way interaction), you need to also include the lower-order/component terms in the same model as predictors of the same things.

So don't just run 

Y ~ PX

Run

Y ~ PX + P1 + P2

If this still doesn't make sense, I suggest hitting up a text like Cohen, Cohen, Aiken, & West's book on multiple regression. It's very clear on how to work with interactions and most of the principles generalize directly to a path/structural framework.

Pat

In a regression framework, if you include a higher-order term (e.g., a two-way interaction), you need to also include the lower-order/component terms in the same model as predictors of the same things.

So don't just run 

Y ~ PX

Run
